subject.title: [Feature] Control UI should accept gateway token from Authorization header

question: Should reverse-proxy shared-secret bootstrap use a short-lived browser session credential, direct WebSocket-upgrade header authentication, or remain unsupported in favor of trusted-proxy identity mode?
rationale: Each option changes how proxy-controlled headers become full Gateway operator authority, and source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent trust and credential-lifetime policy.

options.title: Issue short-lived session
options.body: Validate the injected secret behind explicit proxy and origin checks, then mint a short-lived browser credential bound to the Control UI session and device.

options.title: Authenticate upgrade header
options.body: Accept the shared secret directly on the WebSocket upgrade only from configured trusted proxies while retaining origin, pairing, and rate-limit enforcement.

options.title: Use trusted-proxy identity
options.body: Keep shared-secret headers unsupported and document `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"` as the canonical reverse-proxy authentication model.

recommendation.title: Issue short-lived session
recommendation.body: Validate the injected secret behind explicit proxy and origin checks, then mint a short-lived browser credential bound to the Control UI session and device.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history and prior issue review connect steipete most strongly to Control UI authentication architecture and this exact decision.
